criteria.name: Q1 Quality attributes
criteria.reasoning: Performance scenario is six-part with measurable p95. Availability scenario has six parts but response measure is vague and unmeasurable, matching Proficient descriptor.

evidence.quote: the system should stay up most of the time.

criteria.name: Q2 Architectural style
criteria.reasoning: Modular monolith clearly recommended with two scenario-specific trade-offs team size and single-VM plus deployment downtime, downside acknowledged.

evidence.quote: a bug in one module can still crash the whole process.

criteria.name: Q3 Availability calculation
criteria.reasoning: (a) series product 99.30% and (b) 5.0h correct with working. (c) parallel payment 0.999975 correct but failed to multiply by other components, so end-to-end and downtime wrong. One part incorrect.

evidence.quote: So the new availability of placing an order is 99.9975%

criteria.name: Q4 Resilience pattern
criteria.reasoning: Circuit Breaker correctly explained with Closed/Open/Half-Open, applied to 25-min outage, tuning threshold and timeout given.

evidence.quote: When failures exceed a threshold (for example 50% of calls in 10 seconds)

criteria.name: Q5 Consistency and availability
criteria.reasoning: Both choices reasonable with concrete techniques Redis TTL and idempotency key, but CAP misused partitions cannot be given up, must choose C or A.

evidence.quote: we choose consistency and availability and give up partition tolerance.

criteria.name: Q6 Architecture decision record
criteria.reasoning: Context and Decision specific to OrderPaid RabbitMQ, but Consequences list only positives, no negative consequence like ops complexity or consistency delay.

evidence.quote: The queue also smooths the lunch peak because the workers process orders at a steady rate.

criteria.name: Communication and format
criteria.reasoning: Headings and IEEE references present and writing clear, but Question 2 exceeds 150-word limit at ~180 words.

evidence.quote: I recommend against a full microservices rewrite for the next 12 months.

technical_issues.issue: Part (c) omits series components: correct end-to-end is ~0.99798 = 99.80% and ~1.5h downtime, not 99.9975% and 0.018h.
CAP error: cannot choose C+A and abandon P during partition; partition tolerance is mandatory.
Availability response measure 'stay up most of the time' is not measurable; needs %/time bound.
No negative consequence stated for queue introduction.

overall: Solid scenario-grounded answers with correct series math and patterns, weakened by Q3c recombination error, CAP misunderstanding, and one-sided ADR.

feedback.summary: You wrote clear scenario-grounded answers with strong Q2 and Q4. To reach Excellent, tighten measurability in Q1, correct Q3c recombination, fix CAP reasoning in Q5, add a negative consequence in Q6, and meet word limits.
next_steps: Make your Q1 availability response measurable with a % and time bound, e.g. uptime % per month.
Recalculate Q3c end-to-end as series of all components including redundant payment, then derive downtime.
Correct CAP to choose C or A under partition, add one negative ADR consequence, and trim Q2 under 150 words.

criteria.C1: Well done in Q1: you chose relevant attributes and gave a full six-part performance scenario with measurable p95. For Excellent, rewrite your availability response 'stay up most of the time' as measurable, e.g. % uptime per month.
criteria.C2: Excellent in Q2: you clearly recommended modular monolith with scenario-specific team-size and single-VM trade-offs and acknowledged downtime risk that a bug 'can still crash the whole process'. Keep this specificity.
criteria.C3: Well done in Q3: your (a) 99.30% series and (b) 5.0h downtime with working were correct. For Excellent, fix (c): you reported 99.9975% for payment alone, multiply it by other components for end-to-end ~99.80%.
criteria.C4: Excellent in Q4: you correctly explained Circuit Breaker Closed/Open/Half-Open, applied it to the 25-min outage, and gave tuning of '50% of calls in 10 seconds'. Keep linking mechanism to scenario.
criteria.C5: Good in Q5: reasonable choices with concrete Redis TTL and idempotency key. For Excellent, fix CAP: you wrote 'give up partition tolerance' but you must retain P and choose C or A during partition.
criteria.C6: Good in Q6: specific Context and Decision on OrderPaid RabbitMQ and positive smoothing of 'lunch peak'. For Excellent, add at least one negative consequence such as ops complexity or delay.
criteria.C7: Clear writing with headings and IEEE references. For Excellent, bring every answer within 150 words: Q2 at ~180 words starting 'I recommend against a full microservices rewrite' exceeds the limit.
